chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Offer from a bandleader in St. Louis and the DeShon band
summary: A band leader offered him a place in St. Louis after quarrelling with his pianist Cecil Scott; St. Louis and Kansas City were jazz meccas, and he played briefly with a creole bandleader.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: And of course the musicians who played music were fortunate enough to make a little money, have fun. And this is really what music was about, as far as jazz music was concerned, during that period. And it was, as I said, through meeting these musicians, coming through Cape (crossed out) Granby Jurado, Missouri, while in the CCC Camp, that I got an offer from one of these leaders to come to St. Louis, to play. Because he had had an argument with the piano player, his name was Cecil Scott, and he was a famous -- Tenor saxophone player. (Unintelligible).
I don't -- all I remember about him is that he directed the band. This is another Cecil Scott, I think.
And St. Louis, incidently, and Kansas City, were known jazz meccas. They were the known headquarters in the midwest for excellent jazz players. Many bands -- and
I remember another band I played with after I got there was DeShon Joe O. Shans, and they played all kinds of orchestrations. They were really professional musicians.
I think he was creole birth.
Many of the creoles had a great influence on jazz music, the beginning of jazz, you see. And many of those creole people were great organizers, also.
Did you play in that band?
